chunks: As for what Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from some of his companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), he said:
Condolences (ta'ziya) to the bereaved family [are given] after the burial.
The proper approach to this narration is to interpret it as indicating merit and recommendation (istihbab).

key_terms.التَّعْزِيَةُ: ta'ziya — the act of condolence; consoling the bereaved family after a death
key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: istihbab — the juridical category of recommended (mustahabb); meritorious but not obligatory
key_terms.الْفَضْلِ: fadl — merit, virtue, excellence; indicates a praiseworthy act carrying extra reward
key_terms.الْمُصِيبَةِ: calamity/affliction; here specifically the death of a family member

ai.seo_question: When should ta'ziya (condolences) be offered to the bereaved — before or after the burial of the deceased?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted via Ibn Abi Umayr from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), states that ta'ziya to the bereaved should be given after burial. Sheikh al-Tusi reconciles this with other narrations by ruling that it indicates the meritorious and recommended (mustahabb) nature of post-burial condolences — not that pre-burial condolences are impermissible.
